correctness.reason: The Fourier support-function proof reconstructs the exact coefficient \(2\pi\), the sharpness family, and the equality obstruction without relying on finite experiments.

originality.reason: Inspected prior work gives weaker existential-disk Hausdorff stability or L2 Steiner-disk control, not the sharp canonical Hausdorff theorem. A stronger SCOPE result is dated one day later.

value.reason: This is a sharp canonical stability theorem for a classical constant-width extremal problem.

checked_sources.title: Stability Theorems for Convex Domains of Constant Width
Sharp angular support stability for planar bodies of constant width

final_claim: For planar convex bodies of constant width \(w\), the area deficit from the disk is at least \(2\pi\) times the squared Hausdorff distance to the Steiner disk; \(2\pi\) is sharp and equality occurs only for the disk.
residual_risks: An equivalent older formulation may exist under different support-function or approximation-theory terminology.
